# Security Rules

> Extends [root AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md). Cross-cutting — load when working on auth, input handling, secrets, or rendering.

## Always

- Load secrets from environment variables or GCP Secret Manager. [MUST]
- Extract `locationId` server-side from JWT/auth context only. [MUST]
- Sanitize with `DOMPurify.sanitize()` before any `v-html` or `innerHTML` assignment. [MUST]
- Apply CSRF protection on all state-changing HTTP endpoints. [MUST]
- Use IAM v2 (`@platform-core/iam-v2`) guards or helper methods on protected routes. [MUST]
- Validate and strip unknown fields on all incoming API payloads (via class-validator). [MUST]
- Verify inbound webhooks with raw-body signatures, replay windows, and event-id dedupe before processing. [MUST]
- Preserve tenant context across service clients, workers, queues, webhooks, frontend API calls, and analytics events. [MUST]
- Bind resource ids back to the trusted tenant context before reading or mutating tenant-owned records. [MUST]
- Rotate exposed secrets immediately and audit for similar patterns in codebase. [MUST]
- Apply OWASP Top 10:2025 and ASVS 5.0.0 requirements to security-sensitive PRs, and apply API, LLM, Agentic Skills, MCP, and NHI overlays when changed files touch those surfaces. [MUST]
- Protected IAM v2 routes must have exact `urlScopeMap` entries for method and route path. [MUST]
- URL-mapped IAM scopes must have matching `scopeConfigs` entries. [MUST]
- New IAM scope configs must not use deprecated migration or legacy role boolean fields. [MUST]
- `whoCanAccessAuthClasses` must describe allowed token classes, not the resource verified by `authConfig.authClass`. [MUST]
- Tenant-owned RBAC changes must include cross-agency and cross-subaccount denial proof. [MUST]
- Privileged bypass flows must include least-privilege authorization, reason capture, and structured audit evidence. [MUST]
- Full autonomous security audit runs must record GHL-AI MCP codemap graph context or an explicit partial/fallback state. [MUST]
- PII/data-transfer audit findings must include source-to-sink inventory, tenant context, transfer boundary, and redaction status. [MUST]
- PII must be redacted, hashed, or omitted before logs, analytics events, MCP context, queues, or other broad-access sinks. [MUST]

## Never

- Never hardcode API keys, passwords, tokens, or private keys in source code. [MUST]
- Never trust `locationId` from client request body, query, or params. [MUST]
- Never use `v-html` without DOMPurify sanitization. [MUST]
- Never expose stack traces or internal error details in API responses. [SHOULD]
- Never log PII (email, phone, name) in structured logs. [SHOULD]

## Prefer

- Prefer `unknown` over `any` for externally typed data — validate before use.
- Prefer explicit allow-lists for CORS origins over wildcards.
- Prefer short-lived tokens with refresh over long-lived tokens.
- Prefer HTTPS-only cookies with `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Strict` for session tokens.

## Verify

- Confirm no hardcoded secrets in changed files (`.env` values, inline strings).
- Confirm all new routes have appropriate IAM guard applied.
- Confirm user-supplied content is sanitized before HTML rendering.
- Confirm async boundaries carry trusted tenant context from auth/server context, not client payloads.
- Confirm routes that accept `locationId` plus separate resource ids or bulk ids validate those resources against the trusted tenant before side effects, and add denial tests for mismatched tenant ownership when behavior changes.
- Confirm AI security review findings include a rule id, file and line, exploit scenario, fix recommendation, and test expectation.
- Confirm protected IAM v2 routes have both URL scope map and scope config coverage.
- Confirm RBAC tests or dashboard evidence include cross-tenant denial cases for tenant-owned resources.
- Confirm privileged bypass paths capture a reason and emit structured audit logs before side effects.
